extracted.intended_audience: attorneys, company registrants, compliance officers, SEC filers, and members of the public who need to locate or comply with Securities and Exchange Commission regulations (Title 17, Chapter II)
extracted.subtask_short: navigating SEC regulations (17 CFR Ch. II)
extracted.subtask_description: Locate and interpret the Securities and Exchange Commission rules compiled in 17 CFR Chapter II (Title 17) — a table-of-contents style index of Parts, Subparts, and Sections governing SEC organization, rulemaking, filings, securities offers, exchanges, investment companies, advisers, and related procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part 200 — Organization; Conduct and Ethics; and Information and Requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Part 200 (200.1 – 200.800) — Organization; Conduct and Ethics; and Information and Requests, including subparts on Organization and Program Management, Disposition of Commission Business, Canons of Ethics, Information and Requests, Code of Behavior Governing Ex Parte Communications Between Persons Outside the Commission and Decisional Employees (200.110–200.114), Plan of Organization and Operation Effective During Emergency Conditions, Privacy regulations, Public Observation of Commission Meetings, Classification/Declassification of National Security Information, Protection of the Environment, Enforcement of Nondiscrimination on the Basis of Handicap, Conduct of Members and Employees, and Commission Information Collection Requirements under the Paperwork Reduction Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contains the organizational, ethical, privacy, and procedural rules that govern Commission operations; lists specific § ranges and subparts (200.1–200.800) for detailed rules such as ex parte communications, privacy, and employee conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part 201 — Rules of Practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Part 201 (201.31 – 201.1106) — Rules of Practice, including regulations pertaining to the Equal Access to Justice Act (201.31–201.60) and Rules of Practice (201.100–201.900), adjustment of civil monetary penalties, and Fair Fund and Disgorgement Plans (201.1001; 201.1100–201.1106).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Governs adjudicatory procedures, hearings, remedies, and practitioner conduct before the Commission; includes availability and use of prescribed forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part 202 — Informal and Other Procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Part 202 (202.1 – 202.190) — Informal and Other Procedures: includes §202.1 General; §202.2 Pre-filing assistance and interpretative advice; §202.3 Processing of filings; §202.3a Instructions for filing fees; §202.4 Facilitating administrative hearings; §202.5 Enforcement activities; §202.6 Adoption, revision, and rescission of rules and regulations of general application; §202.7 Submittals; §202.8 Small entity compliance guides; §202.9 Small entity enforcement penalty reduction policy; §202.10 Policy statement concerning subpoenas to the news media; §202.12 Policy statement concerning cooperation by individuals in investigations and related enforcement actions; etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes informal procedures, pre-filing assistance, staff guidance, small-entity policies, and other administrative policies for interacting with the Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part 203 — Rules Relating to Investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: Part 203 (203.1 – 203.8) — Rules Relating to Investigations, including in general (203.1–203.3) and Formal Investigative Proceedings (203.4–203.8).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets the procedures and standards for Commission investigations and formal investigatory proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part 204 — Rules Relating to Debt Collection
rubrics_metrics.description: Part 204 (204.1 – 204.77) — Rules Relating to Debt Collection, with subparts on Administrative Offset, Salary Offset, Tax Refund Offset, Administrative Wage Garnishment, and Miscellaneous provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prescribes procedures for recovering debts owed to the United States and handling offsets and garnishments related to Commission-administered debts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part 205 — Standards of Professional Conduct for Attorneys Appearing and Practicing Before the Commission
rubrics_metrics.description: Part 205 (205.1 – 205.7) — Standards of Professional Conduct for Attorneys Appearing and Practicing Before the Commission in the Representation of an Issuer, including purpose and scope, definitions, responsibilities of supervisory and subordinate attorneys, sanctions and discipline, and statement that there is no private right of action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies ethical and professional responsibilities and sanctions for attorneys practicing before the SEC in issuer representations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part 209 — Forms Prescribed Under the Commission's Rules of Practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Part 209 (209.0-1 – 209.1) — Forms Prescribed Under the Commission's Rules of Practice, including availability of forms and Form D-A: Disclosure of assets and financial information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies the availability and use of forms required by the Rules of Practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part 210 — Form and Content of and Requirements for Financial Statements (Regulation S-X)
rubrics_metrics.description: Part 210 (210.1-01 – 210.15-01) — Application of Regulation S-X (form and content of financial statements) including definitions, qualifications and reports of accountants (210.2-01 – 210.2-07), general instructions as to financial statements (210.3-01 – 210.3-20), consolidated and combined financial statements (210.3A-01 – 210.3A-04), rules of general application (210.4-01 – 210.4-10), and numerous specialized rules for commercial/industrial companies, registered investment companies, insurance companies, smaller reporting companies, interim financial statements, pro forma information, and schedules (210.5 – 210.15-01).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Governs the form, content, presentation, and supporting schedules for financial statements filed with the Commission; contains many section-level requirements such as qualifications of accountants, consolidated balance sheet rules, presentation and age-of-statements requirements, and special industry provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part 211 — Interpretations Relating to Financial Reporting Matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Part 211 — Interpretative Releases Relating to Financial Reporting Matters, including Financial Reporting Releases, Staff Accounting Bulletins, and Accounting and Auditing Enforcement Releases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collects staff interpretations and guidance relating to financial reporting and accounting matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part 227 — Regulation Crowdfunding, General Rules and Regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Part 227 (227.100 – 227.504) — Regulation Crowdfunding, General Rules and Regulations covering General provisions (227.100), Requirements for Issuers (227.201–227.206), Requirements for Intermediaries (227.300–227.305), Funding Portal Regulation (227.400–227.404), and Miscellaneous Provisions (227.501–227.504).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets disclosure, intermediary, offering, and portal rules for crowdfunding under the Securities Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part 229 — Standard Instructions for Filing Forms (Regulation S-K)
rubrics_metrics.description: Part 229 (229.10 – 229.1610) — Standard Instructions for Filing Forms under the Securities Act, Securities Exchange Act and other Acts — Regulation S-K: includes general provisions, business disclosures, securities of the registrant, financial information, management and certain security holders, registration statement and prospectus provisions, exhibits, miscellaneous, industry guides, roll-up transaction rules, M&A (Regulation M‑A), asset-backed securities (Reg AB), sector-specific disclosure (oil and gas, mining, banking), and special purpose acquisition companies (229.1601–229.1610).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes narrative disclosure requirements (business, management, financial and risk disclosures) used across registration statements and reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part 230 — General Rules and Regulations, Securities Act of 1933
rubrics_metrics.description: Part 230 (230.100 – 230.1001) — General Rules and Regulations under the Securities Act of 1933, containing definitions, business hours, filing fees, inspection of registration statements, non-disclosure rules, communications not deemed prospectuses, notice of proposed registered offerings, generic advertising, various exemptions and definitions (e.g., accredited investor, Regulation A, Regulation D, Regulation C, Regulation S, Reg A-R), and numerous specific rules governing prospectuses, prospectus delivery, exemptions, and offer communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comprehensive set of rules governing offers, registrations, prospectuses, exemptions (Reg D, Reg A, Reg S), definitions (e.g., accredited investor), and related procedures under the Securities Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation D — Rules Governing Limited Offers and Sales Without Registration (within Part 230)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections 230.500 – 230.508 — Regulation D: Use of Regulation D; definitions and terms; general conditions to be met; filing of notice of sales; exemptions for limited offerings (e.g., §230.504, §230.506); disqualifying provisions; insignificant deviations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies conditions and filing requirements for private placements and exemptions from registration under the Securities Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation S — Offers and Sales Made Outside the United States
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections 230.901 – 230.905 — Regulation S: General statement and definitions for offers and sales outside the United States; conditions for offers or sales by issuers, distributors, affiliates, and offshore resales and resale limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a safe harbor for offshore offers and resales that are outside the U.S. securities registration requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and Content of Prospectuses (Part 230 §§230.420–230.433)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections 230.420 – 230.433 — Form and Content of Prospectuses: legibility (230.420), presentation of information (230.421), date of prospectuses, filing and number of copies, summary prospectuses, prospectus use before/after effective date, conditions for post-filing free writing prospectuses, and related prospectus rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies formatting, content, timing, and filing obligations for prospectuses used in registered offerings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation C — Registration (Part 230: §§230.400–230.494)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections 230.400 – 230.494 — Regulation C: Registration rules covering application of the sections, general requirements (230.401–230.419) such as requirements as to proper form, number of copies, paper/printing/language/pagination, confidential treatment, additional information, incorporation by reference, and more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes formalities and content requirements for registration statements and related filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Provisions for Offers and Exemptions (selected within Part 230)
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple sections addressing specific exemptions and offerings: Regulation A (conditional small issues exemption, §230.251–230.346), Regulation A‑R (special exemptions), Regulation E (exemption for securities of small business investment companies), exemptions for cross-border rights offerings and business combinations (§230.800–230.802), and others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each exemption contains scope, offering statement/offering circular requirements, definitions, disqualification provisions, reporting obligations, and suspension/withdrawal rules as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part 232 — Regulation S‑T: General Rules and Regulations for Electronic Filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Part 232 (232.10 – 232.903) — Regulation S‑T: General provisions, required electronic filings, exhibits, liability for transmission errors, prohibited executable code, hardship exemptions, preparation of electronic submissions (EDGAR Filer Manual, signatures, incorporation by reference, graphic/audio/video material, type size and legibility, paper size and binding, marking changed material), interactive data (XBRL interactive data submissions, cover page tagging), modular submissions, and foreign private issuer provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets technical, formatting, and procedural rules for electronic filings via EDGAR and interactive data submissions; includes detailed preparation requirements and interactive data rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: EDGAR Filing and Interactive Data Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections within Part 232 addressing EDGAR functions: persons subject to mandated electronic filing (§232.100 – §232.106), exhibits (§232.102), liability for transmission errors (§232.103), use of HTML and hyperlinks (§232.105), prohibition of executable code (§232.106), interactive data file submissions (§232.405–232.408), cover page XBRL data tagging (§232.406), and interactive data financial report filings (§232.407).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prescribes how to prepare, format, and submit electronic filings and XBRL-tagged interactive financial data and assigns liability and technical constraints for such submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part 239 — Forms Prescribed Under the Securities Act of 1933
rubrics_metrics.description: Part 239 (239.0-1 – 239.900) — Forms for registration statements and forms pertaining to exemptions; availability of forms and various form ranges for specific registration statements and exemptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists the official forms to be used when making filings under the Securities Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part 240 — General Rules and Regulations, Securities Exchange Act of 1934
rubrics_metrics.description: Part 240 (240.0-1 – 240.36a1-2) — General Rules and Regulations under the Exchange Act, covering rules and regulations under the Act and related subparts (including reserved subsections); includes many detailed rules across market regulation, reporting, and exchanges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contains the Exchange Act regulatory framework for exchanges, brokers, dealers, and disclosure obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part 242 — Market Structure and Transaction Rules (Regulation M, SHO, ATS, NMS, SE)
rubrics_metrics.description: Part 242 (242.100 – 242.1007 and beyond) — Includes Regulation M (activities by distribution participants, issuers during distribution, Nasdaq passive market making, stabilizing activities); Regulation SHO (short sale definitions, circuit breaker, borrowing and delivery requirements, close-out); Regulation ATS (definitions, requirements for alternative trading systems, recordkeeping and record preservation); customer margin requirements for security futures; Regulation AC (analyst certification); Regulation NMS (national market system rules including dissemination of transaction reports, order protection rule, minimum pricing increments, consolidated audit trail, access to quotations); Regulation SE (registration and regulation of security‑based swap execution facilities with principles, registration requirements, product listing, execution methods, and enforceability provisions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies market conduct, short sale rules, alternative trading system obligations, analyst certifications, national market system trading/display/dissemination rules, and regulation of swap execution venues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part 270 — Rules Under the Investment Company Act of 1940
rubrics_metrics.description: Part 270 — Rules and sections under the Investment Company Act of 1940, including registration, exemptions (e.g., §270.12b-1 distribution of shares; §270.12d1-1 exemptions for investments in money market funds; §§270.30a-1 annual reports; §270.30a-3 controls and procedures; recordkeeping §§270.31a-1 – 31a-4), liquidity risk management programs (§270.22e-4), custody and bonding rules, sales literature, names and labeling, proxy solicitation (§270.20a-1), pricing and redemption rules (§270.22c-1), among many other sector- and function-specific rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes filing, reporting, operational, custody, liquidity, recordkeeping, disclosure, and exemptive requirements for registered investment companies and related persons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part 274 — Forms Prescribed Under the Investment Company Act of 1940
rubrics_metrics.description: Part 274 (274.0-1 – 274.404) — Availability of forms, subparts for registration statements, forms for reports, other statements, exemptions, and electronic filing forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies and describes forms used by investment companies for registration and periodic reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part 275 — Rules and Regulations, Investment Advisers Act of 1940
rubrics_metrics.description: Part 275 (275.0-2 – 275.222-2) — Rules implementing the Investment Advisers Act: general procedures, references to rules/regulations, requirements of papers and applications, procedures for applications and matters, incorporation by reference, small entity definitions for Regulatory Flexibility Act, rules concerning registration, withdrawal, hardship exemptions, Form ADV and amendments, books and records (275.204-2), delivery of brochures and brochure supplements, reporting by exempt advisors, Form CRS delivery, reporting to private funds, codes of ethics, custody rules, marketing, political contributions, proxy voting, pooled investment vehicles, and related definitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Governs adviser registration, reporting, recordkeeping, disclosure to clients, codes of ethics, custody, and permissible adviser business practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parts 281–302 and Specialty Rules (interpretations, Bretton Woods, international bank reporting, SIPC rules, orderly liquidation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Various Parts covering interpretative releases relating to corporate reorganizations, rules pursuant to Bretton Woods Agreements Act (285.1–285.4), rules related to international financial institutions (Parts 286–290), Rules of the Securities Investor Protection Corporation (Part 300), forms for SIPC (Part 301), and rules for orderly liquidation of covered brokers or dealers (Part 302).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contain institution-specific reporting and procedural requirements, customer claim procedures, liquidation procedures, and related forms and schedules.
